subject: Re: Atlas Therapeutics — network island model & SOC 2 evidence bundle
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@atlasthera.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: security@atlasthera.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Network island model + SOC 2 bundle request for Private deployment

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. Our InfoSec team reviewed the materials and asked for a concise "island model" network diagram that shows how Atlas data flows into a Private deployment, plus a bundled SOC 2 evidence checklist mapped to those diagrams (we need it for our pre-onboarding packet).

Can you include:
- A single-page visual (PNG/PDF) of the deployment island: control plane, data plane, public egress points, and any managed sidecars.
- A short mapping table showing which SOC 2/CC controls are satisfied by each network boundary (e.g., CC6.1 — network partitioning).
- Any known residual risks related to egress/transit through cloud provider NATs or partner connectors.

We attached a template that shows the format they prefer. If possible, can we get a draft by EOD your time? We'd like to review before Friday's supplier review.

Attachments: island-model-sketch.vsdx (example drawing), required_evidence_list.xlsx (Atlas template)

Best,
Elena
Senior Information Security Manager
Atlas Therapeutics
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@atlasthera.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Network island model + SOC 2 bundle request for Private deployment

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Looping in Kimberly and Ben to pull the canonical diagrams and the SOC 2 mapping artifacts.

Quick heads-up on scope: for a Private deployment we produce three diagram layers: 1) logical service boundary (what tenants see), 2) control/data plane partition (how the control plane is isolated from customer data), and 3) egress demarcation (how outbound traffic leaves the island). We'll prepare a single-page consolidated view plus a brief mapping table to the SOC 2 criteria.

Plan:
- Kimberly: draft diagrams + short notes on residual egress risk and mitigations.
- Ben: attach the SOC 2 mapping PDF and a short checklist we can drop into your required_evidence_list.xlsx.
- I will review and consolidate, and send a drive link to the draft by 16:30 PT. If that works, Kevin from Atlas can review in the supplier call on Friday.

Attaching our working checklist: isolation-claims-summary.pdf and a diagram request template to match your sheet.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena@atlasthera.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Network island model + SOC 2 bundle request for Private deployment

Elena / team — attaching a concise set of artifacts. Notes below and attachments included.

Summary notes (high level):
- Logical island: single-tenant VPC per customer for Private deployments, with a dedicated subnet for inference runtime nodes and a separate subnet for control-plane agents. The control-plane is customer-optional (private customers can choose a customer-managed control plane or Redwood-managed private control plane).
- Egress demarcation: outbound flows from runtime nodes are routed to a managed egress gateway that performs ACL filtering and optional NAT (customer can supply their own NGFW in front of the gateway). We mark the canonical egress point on the diagram.
- KV/cache and model artifacts: persisted in an internal, customer-scoped object store with restricted service account access; no control-plane credentials are stored with runtime nodes.
- Residual risks: transient metadata leakage via cloud provider metadata service is mitigated (IMDSv2 enforced) and we have an egress DLP policy available as an add-on. If Atlas wants air-gapped ingestion, we can advise on an S3 pre-staging pattern.

What I attached: diagram_request_template.docx (format we used to author the final one), vpc-fence-config-snippets.txt (example iptables/aws-nacl snippets showing segmentation), egress-policy-table.csv (policy rows mapped to SOC2 criteria).

Next steps: Vivek — if you want, I'll convert the docx + VSDX into a single-page PDF and a PNG callout for their slide. Sending draft to the Drive link Vivek will create.

- Kimberly
Sr. Security Architect, Redwood Inference
